guide.whycantisleep.guide.category.sleep: Why the bed says no, and what to do about it.
Restless, lying down has a chance of a **night terror**, and twice that sleepless. The worse the night would have been, the worse the terror.

Your eyes stick half open and you can't move. Red-black fog rolls through the room, the world goes muffled and warped, and your heart quickens.

A shadow rises from the floor beyond the foot of the bed, its eyes kindling, and comes along the bed towards you. Shadow hands reach up beside you.

It stares, face to face. Then a scream, and your eyes slam shut.

You wake gasping and **shaken**, with nausea and slowness, and the night is scored a **Haunting Nightmare**.

->*Sleep well.*<-

Waking in the morning, half the time you wake with a **sleep effect**: good after a good night, bad after a bad one, and now and then something odd.

Each has a rarity, which sets how often it comes and the color it is named in: **common**, {#C9A227}uncommon{/}, {#2BA3B5}rare{/}, {#B05CC8}epic{/}, {#E07B1F}legendary{/}. The rarer good ones need better nights, the rarer bad ones worse.
guide.whycantisleep.guide.entry.hiding.h:
Run into a hiding spot with something hunting you and you must keep your heart slow. The rest of the screen fades away, a band of smoke opens across it, and *Watch out!* slams in.

Beats cross the **pulse line** from right to left, each a tall spike among smaller waves. Press {key:key.attack} as the spike passes through the **window** in the middle.

Arrows under the window and a soft chime tell you a beat is close. The window breathes while a beat is inside it.

The words over the band say how you're doing. A run of caught beats rings higher and higher, and calms the red veins creeping in round the screen.

Clicking too early or too late, or letting a beat pass, breaks one of your **three hearts**, and the veins creep further in. At the third you **gasp**, and whatever chased you in hears it.

While you keep your heart slow, your moves make no noise and nothing finds you by chance: only your heart can give you away. It lasts until the hide time is up.
Miss the last beat as the time runs out, with monsters still near, and you must catch **one more** before you're safe. It can ask twice, no more.

Hold {key:key.sneak} and use a hiding spot with **empty hands** to get in. Hidden, nothing can see you: whatever was after you loses you.

Stay hidden long enough (**15 seconds**, less with walls close round you) and what chased you in gives up and vanishes in smoke, along with the monsters prowling round the spot, even the ones that kept you from sleeping there.

> They only vanish if every other player nearby is hiding too. Someone out in the open, and they just lose you.

Press {key:key.sneak} again to come out. Being hurt brings you out too, and so does the spot breaking, another player opening it, or being found.

Out of a chest or a closet you stand right in front of it; out of anything else, where you went in.

After coming out you need a moment to catch your breath before you can hide again.

Some aren't fooled, and still see you:

Your eyes narrow to a squint that sways with your breath, tightens when monsters are near, and blinks now and then.

A card says what is out there. With monsters near, its timer counts down how long you must hold out.

You hear what prowls round you: muffled footsteps on whatever they walk on, and their shuffling when they stand.

Sounds from outside reach you **muffled**, as much as the spot shuts them out: walls and doors keep most out, glass less, and an open side lets them in. A door's windows let a little through.

Your own sounds, inside the spot with you, are left as they are.
Learn where to hide, then wait something out.
guide.whycantisleep.guide.entry.hiding.q:
Trying to walk or jump, or swinging the view about, makes **noise**. With monsters near, the card tells you to hold still; keep still and it fades away. With voice chat, your voice is noise too: whisper, or say nothing.

Make too much noise with a monster near the spot and you're **heard**: pulled out, with everything that chased you in coming for you at once.
Now and then a [silverfish](entity:minecraft:silverfish) or a [cave spider](entity:minecraft:cave_spider) is already in the spot, and comes out at you instead.
guide.whycantisleep.guide.entry.hiding.s:
What chased you in doesn't just wander off. After a moment it comes to your spot, stops in front of it and **looks about**, now and then right at you.

Then it either **finds you** and drags you out, or walks away.

The chance it finds you is **25%** on normal, half that on easy, half as much again on hard, and none on peaceful. Noise you make adds to it.

While you're keeping your heart slow it **can't find you by chance**: only failing the heartbeat gives you away.
Another player who opens the chest or closet door you hide behind **finds you**, and you come out in front of them.
Crawl under any bed and lie flat. It needs a **floor** under it: a bed over air turns you away, and breaking the floor brings you out.

Two **top slabs** {slot:minecraft:oak_slab} or **upside-down stairs** {slot:minecraft:oak_stairs} side by side, **carpet** {slot:minecraft:white_carpet} on both and a floor under: a table to hide under.

Climb into a **double chest**; a single one is too small. Its lid stays open a crack, and you peer out through the gap, turning only so far: anyone looking sees your eyes in the dark of it.

A double chest holds **two**, one in each half.
A door, or a double door, with a nook behind it **two blocks high**, shut in on every other side, roof and floor too, with room to stand. The door shuts behind you.

- The nook is one block wide for a door, two for a double door, which holds **two**.
- Walls can be blocks, or **trapdoors** {slot:minecraft:oak_trapdoor} lying flush against the nook: open ones for walls, shut ones for a roof.
- The door must open **out** of the nook: place it from inside, looking out.

> A spot with someone in it, or a monster, can't take another.

Three to build follow, to step through: [one of planks](build:closet), [one walled with trapdoors](build:trapdoor_closet), and [a double closet](build:double_closet) for two.
One door for one; a double door, a nook behind each, for two.
Each soothing thing within six blocks of the bed (three up and down) is worth {#3FA34D}+2{/}, up to {#3FA34D}+10{/}. A potted plant counts as its plant.

Each unsettling thing near the bed is worth {#D9493F}-3{/}, down to {#D9493F}-15{/}.

> Their tooltips say which they are, and what they're worth.
A jukebox playing within 16 blocks counts.

Each night is scored from **0 to 100**, starting at 75, from everything about it: the room, the light, monsters, music, things by the bed, and how you have been sleeping.

In the morning a card shows the score, a word for it and what mattered most:

- {#3FA34D}Great{/} 85 and up, {#3FA34D}Good{/} 65 and up
- {#C9A227}Fair{/} 45 and up
- {#D9493F}Poor{/} 25 and up, {#D9493F}Awful{/} below

Sleep through to morning in a **closed room** that is **lit all through**, doors shut and no dark corners, and you wake well rested, with a little Regeneration.

A room is closed when the air round the bed stays small and never sees the sky.

Refused sleeps in a row and days without lying down add up:

- **Rested**: all is well.
- **Restless**: two refusals, or two days.
- **Sleepless**: five refusals, or three days.

A **moon** in the corner of the screen fills up with each day without sleep, full at three.
Sleepless, the phantoms come for you at night. Restless or worse, a night terror may be waiting when you lie down: see {entry:effects/terrors}.
The moon button on your player in the **inventory** shows how you have been sleeping and how your last night went: its score, what mattered most, and what you woke with.
guide.whycantisleep.guide.entry.sleeping:
With another player online, lying in bed shows the **Bedtime** panel: how many are asleep as a bar, one segment for each sleeper the night needs, and who is still awake and why: awake, mining, fighting, away, or in another dimension.

**Click** an awake player to nudge them: a bell and a message, then a cooldown.

When only one player is still up, those in bed can **vote** from the panel to skip the night.

Once everyone in bed has voted, the players still up are asked in chat: *Go ahead* or *Not yet*. *Not yet* ends the vote for a minute; no answer in 30 seconds skips the night.
A bed within three blocks of another player who is asleep lets a couple of monsters by: sharing a room is braver than sleeping alone.

When monsters keep you from sleeping, exactly the ones that stopped you **glow** for a few seconds, colored by the kind of threat: [creepers](entity:minecraft:creeper), [endermen](entity:minecraft:enderman) and [raiders](entity:minecraft:pillager), [the undead](entity:minecraft:zombie), and the rest each have their own color.

The most dangerous of them, a creeper above all and then the nearest, throbs brighter and gets a larger pointer.

> Only you see the glow.

- **Arrows** around the crosshair point to the ones outside your view.
- A monster in view but **behind blocks** gets a ring where it is, pulsing out like a sound you'd hear.
- They leave **footprints** in their colors where they walked, for a while after the glow is gone.

The card above the hotbar says how many there are and where the closest is: *3 monsters nearby, closest: Zombie, 6 blocks below*.

Lie down and your eyelids grow heavy: half shut, swaying slowly, each blink dropping shut and lifting slowly.

Once everyone the night needs is asleep, or you're on your own, they close, fighting it once, and are shut before the night passes. If someone gets up, they go back to drowsy.

Wake in the morning and they flutter open; get up early and they just open.

As your eyes close the world's sounds sink with them, duller, quieter and a little warped, until asleep you hardly hear a thing. They come back as you wake.

> Hiding muffles what is outside your spot the same way: see {entry:hiding/how}.

A bed that says no always says why, and what to do:

- **Monsters nearby**: deal with them, or hide.
- **Not the time**: beds work at night and in thunderstorms.
- **Too far**: stand next to the bed.
- **Obstructed**: something is in the way above it.
- **Occupied**: someone is already in it.
- **Other players awake**: how many more must sleep.

In the Nether and the End beds explode. The first try only {#D9493F}warns{/}; use it again within three seconds to go through with it.

Deal with every monster that blocked your sleep within **10 seconds**, with nothing else coming near, and the room is safe.

Still standing by the bed, you lie straight down in it.

> The monsters still count until they are gone, so a dying one keeps you up a moment longer.
